svg.text: A fetcher retrieves the bytes behind a URL and nothing else. Consumer-owned, one module per transport or host -- never per format.
1 - WHICH FETCHER RETRIEVES THIS URL (resolved once, at fux add)
Written once by fux add; a line without
it fails to load. Every line is a pin --
a route changed later does not move it;
fux doctor reports the drift instead.
Key is the HOST: host, *.host, host:port,
or a re: pattern. Literal order is
matching one host is a HARD ERROR.
Drop a file in and it works. Read from
doctor stays offline and a consumer's
The shipped http.py / cdp.py claim nothing.
THERE IS NO DEFAULT LAYER (W-199 D2).
--fetch not given, no route, no claim -> fux add REFUSES, printing the hosts it tried and the fetcher stems on disk. [sources.url] fetcher is gone.
def fetch(url: str) -> tuple[bytes, str]: ... # (bytes, Content-Type)
def validate(url: str) -> str | None # ETag / Last-Modified token
Retrieval only. A fetcher that returned Markdown made the index depend on WHICH fetcher ran (W-86 P8).
raise FetcherError -> this URL is SKIPPED, run continues
err.rate_limited -> the host backs off, not the run
validate() same -> body fetch skipped; sha still compared
Fux never sees a status code. The fetcher speaks HTTP (or CDP, or your API); the engine does not.
3 - WHERE A FETCHER SITS IN INGEST (one URL line, left to right)
one sorted line per document; no clock (L3)
* Today the engine picks the decoder from the
Content-Type header, then the URL extension.
W-199 DoD 10 (pending) makes the line's declared
4 - THE SAME PAIR AT ANSWER TIME (the refer plane)
fux answer cites a URL -> the SAME pinned fetcher re-fetches it, the SAME declared decoder re-decodes it, a fresh sha is compared.
Verdict: current . stale . cached (TTL) . unverified. This is why the pairing lives on the committed line and not inside a fetcher's code.
A fetcher is keyed on WHERE (transport, host); a decoder on WHAT (format).
One cdp fetcher serves .xlsx, .html and .pdf alike; the line pairs them. There is no "xlsx fetcher".
A link found inside a decoded page is an EDGE, never a fetch.
It becomes a ref edge if its target is already in the index; otherwise nothing. The corpus is the list.

Following links at ingest would make the index depend on a crawl frontier (L3), reach beyond the fenced list (L4) and index pages nobody declared (L2). Discovery, if wanted, is a fux add feature that writes lines.
Drawn from src/fux/ingest/urlsrc.py, routes.py, register.py and .fux/fetchers/http.py, 2026-09-21. SR-FETCHER - SR-URL-LIST - SR-CONFIG - SR-REFER-PLANE. W-199 DoD 10 pending.
